name: FL-17

key_factors: R+10 district with incumbent Greg Steube seeking re-election

model.rationale: Steube holds a Republican-leaning district with a dominant fundraising edge and no serious outside spending against him, while markets price his re-election around 95%. The Democratic challenger's minimal war chest leaves little evidence to move off the fundamentals-based expectation of a double-digit Republican win.
model.watch: Any late polling, outside spending, or redistricting change showing the district moving toward the center would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Greg Steube seeks re-election in a southwest Florida district that leans Republican by about ten points. He is well funded, with more than $2 million on hand, while Democrat Matthew Montavon has raised under $100,000 and has minimal cash remaining. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but has shown little financial activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets give Steube roughly a 95% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Republican, with a wide but not absolute margin reflecting the usual uncertainty in low-information contests.
